CIO — firm conclusion
BOTTOM LINE: trade the gaps between the lenses, harvest breadth, refuse crowds and lone-ARM heroics. TOP ACTIONABLES: (1) VEDL -- firm-wide hold-underweight, do-not-add across all desks until flow reverses; flow (-13,051cr) is the leading signal over ARM 70. (2) LT -- sanctioned active underweight to mandate (Q4 fade), capped by each desk's TE budget, deepest in thematic Infra. (3) BHARTIARTL -- hold CORE on +Rs8,521cr flow + rising ARM + FII; NO overweight in concentrated/Focused books until the optical-PAT delta is confirmed. (4) LICI -- wait for flow; benchmark-weight everywhere except a tiny starter in the Value contra book. (5) Cap cross-desk SOLAR concentration (Premier/Waaree/Solar Inds) at the firm level; Mid Cap correctly declines, Infra holds capped. (6) OVERWEIGHT the Core Equity breadth engine (Multicap/Flexi) and the Healthcare confirm-breadth (Pharma desk); express LT/WIPRO/VEDL as the firm's coordinated underweights. Every overweight must be a triple-confirmed Q1 name sized as breadth -- the portfolio is the edge, no single name is.

How to read the firm track
A digital firm = one paper book per distinct equity/hybrid scheme of that AMC, each run by the deterministic rules-FM under its own SEBI mandate + liquidity caps (paper-money, no look-ahead, free — no LLM). Firm AUM = Σ each scheme's real AUM. Beat bench · paper = desks whose paper-track CAGR exceeds their benchmark TR since 2015.
★ Read the historical track honestly: a true SECTOR/THEME fund (Banking, Pharma, Digital, Consumption, Transport, Manufacturing, Infra) is now theme-fenced — its 2015→ replay picks ONLY from its own sector(s), and is scored against its sector TR index (NIFTY Healthcare / Financial Services / India Manufacturing …), which removes the broad-market sector beta that made every thematic desk look alike. A residual high IR on some desks (e.g. Digital, Transport) is NOT certified pure stock-selection alpha — the rules-FM is NOT cap-weight-constrained, so within the sector it tilts to smid + momentum names that beat the cap-weighted sector index; that is a factor tilt vs the index, read it as such (Banking, IR ~0.45, is the honest baseline). Diversified mandates (Large/Flexi/Value/Multi-Cap/Small…) select from the broad market vs their broad benchmark, as they should. Characteristic themes (PSU/MNC/ESG/Business-Cycle) are defined by ownership/style, not a sector — with no point-in-time eligibility flag they stay on the broad universe vs NIFTY 500, so their excess still carries some style beta (flagged, a known limitation). The current fact sheet / holdings (the seam book) IS each scheme's real disclosed portfolio — theme-faithful.

Plain-English read — Fundamental Law of Active Management: IR = IC · √breadth · TC
  • IR +0.20 — the book edges its benchmark: it earned +1.53% excess CAGR per 7.6% of tracking error.
  • IC +0.047 (t 5.0) — the selection signal is genuinely informative; ~0.05 is a good single-name forecast correlation.
  • TC 0.77 — about 76% of the raw signal survives the long-only / position-cap constraints (the rest is the implementation leak).
IC = mean cross-sectional Spearman(ARM score, next-rebalance return) over the candidate universe; TC = mean corr(actual target weights, unconstrained score-weights); BR is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are NOT independent — true breadth is far lower), so implied_IR is an upper bound on what the signal could deliver, to be read against the realized IR.
Definitions — IC · Breadth · TC · IR
IC (information coefficient) = the rank correlation between the signal's forecast and the realised next-period return, per bet — how often the call is right. Breadth (BR) = the number of independent bets per year — more, de-correlated bets compound skill. TC (transfer coefficient) = the fraction of that skill that actually reaches the live portfolio after long-only and position-size constraints. IR (information ratio) = excess return ÷ tracking error — the realised skill the law predicts as IC·√BR·TC. Breadth here is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are not independent), so implied IR is a ceiling, not a forecast.

Plain-English read — Fundamental Law of Active Management: IR = IC · √breadth · TC
  • IR +0.45 — the book adds value over its benchmark: it earned +6.26% excess CAGR per 13.8% of tracking error.
  • IC +0.073 (t 4.0) — the selection signal is genuinely informative; ~0.05 is a good single-name forecast correlation.
  • TC 0.78 — about 78% of the raw signal survives the long-only / position-cap constraints (the rest is the implementation leak).
  • vs real Aditya Birla Sun Life Banking and Financial Services Fund - Direct Plan - Growth — the paper book ran 5.36% ahead of the actual fund over 11.4 years.
IC = mean cross-sectional Spearman(ARM score, next-rebalance return) over the candidate universe; TC = mean corr(actual target weights, unconstrained score-weights); BR is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are NOT independent — true breadth is far lower), so implied_IR is an upper bound on what the signal could deliver, to be read against the realized IR.
Definitions — IC · Breadth · TC · IR
IC (information coefficient) = the rank correlation between the signal's forecast and the realised next-period return, per bet — how often the call is right. Breadth (BR) = the number of independent bets per year — more, de-correlated bets compound skill. TC (transfer coefficient) = the fraction of that skill that actually reaches the live portfolio after long-only and position-size constraints. IR (information ratio) = excess return ÷ tracking error — the realised skill the law predicts as IC·√BR·TC. Breadth here is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are not independent), so implied IR is a ceiling, not a forecast.

Plain-English read — Fundamental Law of Active Management: IR = IC · √breadth · TC
  • IR +0.59 — the book adds value over its benchmark: it earned +9.69% excess CAGR per 16.4% of tracking error.
  • IC +0.044 (t 4.7) — the selection signal is genuinely informative; ~0.05 is a good single-name forecast correlation.
  • TC 0.45 — about 45% of the raw signal survives the long-only / position-cap constraints (the rest is the implementation leak).
  • vs real Aditya Birla Sun Life Business Cycle Fund-Direct Growth — the paper book ran 5.55% ahead of the actual fund over 4.5 years.
IC = mean cross-sectional Spearman(ARM score, next-rebalance return) over the candidate universe; TC = mean corr(actual target weights, unconstrained score-weights); BR is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are NOT independent — true breadth is far lower), so implied_IR is an upper bound on what the signal could deliver, to be read against the realized IR.
Definitions — IC · Breadth · TC · IR
IC (information coefficient) = the rank correlation between the signal's forecast and the realised next-period return, per bet — how often the call is right. Breadth (BR) = the number of independent bets per year — more, de-correlated bets compound skill. TC (transfer coefficient) = the fraction of that skill that actually reaches the live portfolio after long-only and position-size constraints. IR (information ratio) = excess return ÷ tracking error — the realised skill the law predicts as IC·√BR·TC. Breadth here is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are not independent), so implied IR is a ceiling, not a forecast.

Plain-English read — Fundamental Law of Active Management: IR = IC · √breadth · TC
  • IR +0.59 — the book adds value over its benchmark: it earned +9.70% excess CAGR per 16.4% of tracking error.
  • IC +0.044 (t 4.7) — the selection signal is genuinely informative; ~0.05 is a good single-name forecast correlation.
  • TC 0.45 — about 45% of the raw signal survives the long-only / position-cap constraints (the rest is the implementation leak).
  • vs real Aditya Birla Sun Life Conglomerate Fund-Direct Growth — the paper book ran 17.52% behind the actual fund over 1.5 years.
IC = mean cross-sectional Spearman(ARM score, next-rebalance return) over the candidate universe; TC = mean corr(actual target weights, unconstrained score-weights); BR is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are NOT independent — true breadth is far lower), so implied_IR is an upper bound on what the signal could deliver, to be read against the realized IR.
Definitions — IC · Breadth · TC · IR
IC (information coefficient) = the rank correlation between the signal's forecast and the realised next-period return, per bet — how often the call is right. Breadth (BR) = the number of independent bets per year — more, de-correlated bets compound skill. TC (transfer coefficient) = the fraction of that skill that actually reaches the live portfolio after long-only and position-size constraints. IR (information ratio) = excess return ÷ tracking error — the realised skill the law predicts as IC·√BR·TC. Breadth here is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are not independent), so implied IR is a ceiling, not a forecast.

Plain-English read — Fundamental Law of Active Management: IR = IC · √breadth · TC
  • IR +1.08 — the book adds value over its benchmark: it earned +16.98% excess CAGR per 15.7% of tracking error.
  • IC +0.065 (t 6.2) — the selection signal is genuinely informative; ~0.05 is a good single-name forecast correlation.
  • TC 0.56 — about 56% of the raw signal survives the long-only / position-cap constraints (the rest is the implementation leak).
  • vs real Aditya Birla Sun Life Consumption Fund - Growth - Direct Plan — the paper book ran 15.58% ahead of the actual fund over 11.4 years.
IC = mean cross-sectional Spearman(ARM score, next-rebalance return) over the candidate universe; TC = mean corr(actual target weights, unconstrained score-weights); BR is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are NOT independent — true breadth is far lower), so implied_IR is an upper bound on what the signal could deliver, to be read against the realized IR.
Definitions — IC · Breadth · TC · IR
IC (information coefficient) = the rank correlation between the signal's forecast and the realised next-period return, per bet — how often the call is right. Breadth (BR) = the number of independent bets per year — more, de-correlated bets compound skill. TC (transfer coefficient) = the fraction of that skill that actually reaches the live portfolio after long-only and position-size constraints. IR (information ratio) = excess return ÷ tracking error — the realised skill the law predicts as IC·√BR·TC. Breadth here is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are not independent), so implied IR is a ceiling, not a forecast.

Plain-English read — Fundamental Law of Active Management: IR = IC · √breadth · TC
  • IR +1.43 — the book adds value over its benchmark: it earned +14.81% excess CAGR per 10.3% of tracking error.
  • IC +0.034 (t 6.9) — the selection signal is genuinely informative; ~0.05 is a good single-name forecast correlation.
  • TC 0.45 — about 44% of the raw signal survives the long-only / position-cap constraints (the rest is the implementation leak).
IC = mean cross-sectional Spearman(ARM score, next-rebalance return) over the candidate universe; TC = mean corr(actual target weights, unconstrained score-weights); BR is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are NOT independent — true breadth is far lower), so implied_IR is an upper bound on what the signal could deliver, to be read against the realized IR.
Definitions — IC · Breadth · TC · IR
IC (information coefficient) = the rank correlation between the signal's forecast and the realised next-period return, per bet — how often the call is right. Breadth (BR) = the number of independent bets per year — more, de-correlated bets compound skill. TC (transfer coefficient) = the fraction of that skill that actually reaches the live portfolio after long-only and position-size constraints. IR (information ratio) = excess return ÷ tracking error — the realised skill the law predicts as IC·√BR·TC. Breadth here is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are not independent), so implied IR is a ceiling, not a forecast.

Plain-English read — Fundamental Law of Active Management: IR = IC · √breadth · TC
  • IR +0.60 — the book adds value over its benchmark: it earned +8.08% excess CAGR per 13.5% of tracking error.
  • IC +0.042 (t 4.9) — the selection signal is genuinely informative; ~0.05 is a good single-name forecast correlation.
  • TC 0.38 — about 38% of the raw signal survives the long-only / position-cap constraints (the rest is the implementation leak).
  • vs real Aditya Birla Sun Life ELSS Tax Saver Fund - Growth - Direct Plan — the paper book ran 9.63% ahead of the actual fund over 11.4 years.
IC = mean cross-sectional Spearman(ARM score, next-rebalance return) over the candidate universe; TC = mean corr(actual target weights, unconstrained score-weights); BR is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are NOT independent — true breadth is far lower), so implied_IR is an upper bound on what the signal could deliver, to be read against the realized IR.
Definitions — IC · Breadth · TC · IR
IC (information coefficient) = the rank correlation between the signal's forecast and the realised next-period return, per bet — how often the call is right. Breadth (BR) = the number of independent bets per year — more, de-correlated bets compound skill. TC (transfer coefficient) = the fraction of that skill that actually reaches the live portfolio after long-only and position-size constraints. IR (information ratio) = excess return ÷ tracking error — the realised skill the law predicts as IC·√BR·TC. Breadth here is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are not independent), so implied IR is a ceiling, not a forecast.

Plain-English read — Fundamental Law of Active Management: IR = IC · √breadth · TC
  • IR +0.57 — the book adds value over its benchmark: it earned +4.28% excess CAGR per 7.5% of tracking error.
  • IC +0.047 (t 5.0) — the selection signal is genuinely informative; ~0.05 is a good single-name forecast correlation.
  • TC 0.77 — about 77% of the raw signal survives the long-only / position-cap constraints (the rest is the implementation leak).
IC = mean cross-sectional Spearman(ARM score, next-rebalance return) over the candidate universe; TC = mean corr(actual target weights, unconstrained score-weights); BR is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are NOT independent — true breadth is far lower), so implied_IR is an upper bound on what the signal could deliver, to be read against the realized IR.
Definitions — IC · Breadth · TC · IR
IC (information coefficient) = the rank correlation between the signal's forecast and the realised next-period return, per bet — how often the call is right. Breadth (BR) = the number of independent bets per year — more, de-correlated bets compound skill. TC (transfer coefficient) = the fraction of that skill that actually reaches the live portfolio after long-only and position-size constraints. IR (information ratio) = excess return ÷ tracking error — the realised skill the law predicts as IC·√BR·TC. Breadth here is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are not independent), so implied IR is a ceiling, not a forecast.

Plain-English read — Fundamental Law of Active Management: IR = IC · √breadth · TC
  • IR -0.39 — the book lags its benchmark: it earned -4.02% excess CAGR per 10.2% of tracking error.
  • IC +0.047 (t 5.0) — the selection signal is genuinely informative; ~0.05 is a good single-name forecast correlation.
  • TC 0.76 — about 76% of the raw signal survives the long-only / position-cap constraints (the rest is the implementation leak).
IC = mean cross-sectional Spearman(ARM score, next-rebalance return) over the candidate universe; TC = mean corr(actual target weights, unconstrained score-weights); BR is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are NOT independent — true breadth is far lower), so implied_IR is an upper bound on what the signal could deliver, to be read against the realized IR.
Definitions — IC · Breadth · TC · IR
IC (information coefficient) = the rank correlation between the signal's forecast and the realised next-period return, per bet — how often the call is right. Breadth (BR) = the number of independent bets per year — more, de-correlated bets compound skill. TC (transfer coefficient) = the fraction of that skill that actually reaches the live portfolio after long-only and position-size constraints. IR (information ratio) = excess return ÷ tracking error — the realised skill the law predicts as IC·√BR·TC. Breadth here is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are not independent), so implied IR is a ceiling, not a forecast.

Plain-English read — Fundamental Law of Active Management: IR = IC · √breadth · TC
  • IR +0.62 — the book adds value over its benchmark: it earned +9.87% excess CAGR per 15.8% of tracking error.
  • IC +0.044 (t 4.7) — the selection signal is genuinely informative; ~0.05 is a good single-name forecast correlation.
  • TC 0.54 — about 54% of the raw signal survives the long-only / position-cap constraints (the rest is the implementation leak).
  • vs real Aditya Birla Sun Life ESG Integration Strategy Fund-Direct Plan-Growth — the paper book ran 11.58% ahead of the actual fund over 5.5 years.
IC = mean cross-sectional Spearman(ARM score, next-rebalance return) over the candidate universe; TC = mean corr(actual target weights, unconstrained score-weights); BR is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are NOT independent — true breadth is far lower), so implied_IR is an upper bound on what the signal could deliver, to be read against the realized IR.
Definitions — IC · Breadth · TC · IR
IC (information coefficient) = the rank correlation between the signal's forecast and the realised next-period return, per bet — how often the call is right. Breadth (BR) = the number of independent bets per year — more, de-correlated bets compound skill. TC (transfer coefficient) = the fraction of that skill that actually reaches the live portfolio after long-only and position-size constraints. IR (information ratio) = excess return ÷ tracking error — the realised skill the law predicts as IC·√BR·TC. Breadth here is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are not independent), so implied IR is a ceiling, not a forecast.

Plain-English read — Fundamental Law of Active Management: IR = IC · √breadth · TC
  • IR +0.53 — the book adds value over its benchmark: it earned +6.59% excess CAGR per 12.5% of tracking error.
  • IC +0.042 (t 4.9) — the selection signal is genuinely informative; ~0.05 is a good single-name forecast correlation.
  • TC 0.38 — about 38% of the raw signal survives the long-only / position-cap constraints (the rest is the implementation leak).
  • vs real Aditya Birla Sun Life Flexi Cap Fund - Growth - Direct Plan — the paper book ran 5.08% ahead of the actual fund over 11.4 years.
IC = mean cross-sectional Spearman(ARM score, next-rebalance return) over the candidate universe; TC = mean corr(actual target weights, unconstrained score-weights); BR is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are NOT independent — true breadth is far lower), so implied_IR is an upper bound on what the signal could deliver, to be read against the realized IR.
Definitions — IC · Breadth · TC · IR
IC (information coefficient) = the rank correlation between the signal's forecast and the realised next-period return, per bet — how often the call is right. Breadth (BR) = the number of independent bets per year — more, de-correlated bets compound skill. TC (transfer coefficient) = the fraction of that skill that actually reaches the live portfolio after long-only and position-size constraints. IR (information ratio) = excess return ÷ tracking error — the realised skill the law predicts as IC·√BR·TC. Breadth here is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are not independent), so implied IR is a ceiling, not a forecast.

IC = mean cross-sectional Spearman(ARM score, next-rebalance return) over the candidate universe; TC = mean corr(actual target weights, unconstrained score-weights); BR is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are NOT independent — true breadth is far lower), so implied_IR is an upper bound on what the signal could deliver, to be read against the realized IR.
Definitions — IC · Breadth · TC · IR
IC (information coefficient) = the rank correlation between the signal's forecast and the realised next-period return, per bet — how often the call is right. Breadth (BR) = the number of independent bets per year — more, de-correlated bets compound skill. TC (transfer coefficient) = the fraction of that skill that actually reaches the live portfolio after long-only and position-size constraints. IR (information ratio) = excess return ÷ tracking error — the realised skill the law predicts as IC·√BR·TC. Breadth here is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are not independent), so implied IR is a ceiling, not a forecast.

IC = mean cross-sectional Spearman(ARM score, next-rebalance return) over the candidate universe; TC = mean corr(actual target weights, unconstrained score-weights); BR is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are NOT independent — true breadth is far lower), so implied_IR is an upper bound on what the signal could deliver, to be read against the realized IR.
Definitions — IC · Breadth · TC · IR
IC (information coefficient) = the rank correlation between the signal's forecast and the realised next-period return, per bet — how often the call is right. Breadth (BR) = the number of independent bets per year — more, de-correlated bets compound skill. TC (transfer coefficient) = the fraction of that skill that actually reaches the live portfolio after long-only and position-size constraints. IR (information ratio) = excess return ÷ tracking error — the realised skill the law predicts as IC·√BR·TC. Breadth here is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are not independent), so implied IR is a ceiling, not a forecast.

Plain-English read — Fundamental Law of Active Management: IR = IC · √breadth · TC
  • IR +0.62 — the book adds value over its benchmark: it earned +6.19% excess CAGR per 10.0% of tracking error.
  • IC +0.037 (t 3.1) — the selection signal is genuinely informative; ~0.05 is a good single-name forecast correlation.
  • TC 0.82 — about 82% of the raw signal survives the long-only / position-cap constraints (the rest is the implementation leak).
  • vs real Aditya Birla Sun Life Large & Mid Cap Fund - Growth - Direct Plan — the paper book ran 8.53% ahead of the actual fund over 11.4 years.
IC = mean cross-sectional Spearman(ARM score, next-rebalance return) over the candidate universe; TC = mean corr(actual target weights, unconstrained score-weights); BR is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are NOT independent — true breadth is far lower), so implied_IR is an upper bound on what the signal could deliver, to be read against the realized IR.
Definitions — IC · Breadth · TC · IR
IC (information coefficient) = the rank correlation between the signal's forecast and the realised next-period return, per bet — how often the call is right. Breadth (BR) = the number of independent bets per year — more, de-correlated bets compound skill. TC (transfer coefficient) = the fraction of that skill that actually reaches the live portfolio after long-only and position-size constraints. IR (information ratio) = excess return ÷ tracking error — the realised skill the law predicts as IC·√BR·TC. Breadth here is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are not independent), so implied IR is a ceiling, not a forecast.

Plain-English read — Fundamental Law of Active Management: IR = IC · √breadth · TC
  • IR +0.28 — the book edges its benchmark: it earned +2.80% excess CAGR per 10.1% of tracking error.
  • IC +0.037 (t 2.4) — the selection signal is genuinely informative; ~0.05 is a good single-name forecast correlation.
  • TC 0.89 — about 89% of the raw signal survives the long-only / position-cap constraints (the rest is the implementation leak).
  • vs real Aditya Birla Sun Life Large & Mid Cap Fund - Growth - Direct Plan — the paper book ran 2.22% ahead of the actual fund over 11.4 years.
IC = mean cross-sectional Spearman(ARM score, next-rebalance return) over the candidate universe; TC = mean corr(actual target weights, unconstrained score-weights); BR is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are NOT independent — true breadth is far lower), so implied_IR is an upper bound on what the signal could deliver, to be read against the realized IR.
Definitions — IC · Breadth · TC · IR
IC (information coefficient) = the rank correlation between the signal's forecast and the realised next-period return, per bet — how often the call is right. Breadth (BR) = the number of independent bets per year — more, de-correlated bets compound skill. TC (transfer coefficient) = the fraction of that skill that actually reaches the live portfolio after long-only and position-size constraints. IR (information ratio) = excess return ÷ tracking error — the realised skill the law predicts as IC·√BR·TC. Breadth here is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are not independent), so implied IR is a ceiling, not a forecast.

Plain-English read — Fundamental Law of Active Management: IR = IC · √breadth · TC
  • IR +1.67 — the book adds value over its benchmark: it earned +19.16% excess CAGR per 11.4% of tracking error.
  • IC +0.054 (t 5.3) — the selection signal is genuinely informative; ~0.05 is a good single-name forecast correlation.
  • TC 0.69 — about 69% of the raw signal survives the long-only / position-cap constraints (the rest is the implementation leak).
  • vs real Aditya Birla Sun Life Manufacturing Equity Fund - Direct Plan - Growth — the paper book ran 19.12% ahead of the actual fund over 11.4 years.
IC = mean cross-sectional Spearman(ARM score, next-rebalance return) over the candidate universe; TC = mean corr(actual target weights, unconstrained score-weights); BR is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are NOT independent — true breadth is far lower), so implied_IR is an upper bound on what the signal could deliver, to be read against the realized IR.
Definitions — IC · Breadth · TC · IR
IC (information coefficient) = the rank correlation between the signal's forecast and the realised next-period return, per bet — how often the call is right. Breadth (BR) = the number of independent bets per year — more, de-correlated bets compound skill. TC (transfer coefficient) = the fraction of that skill that actually reaches the live portfolio after long-only and position-size constraints. IR (information ratio) = excess return ÷ tracking error — the realised skill the law predicts as IC·√BR·TC. Breadth here is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are not independent), so implied IR is a ceiling, not a forecast.

Plain-English read — Fundamental Law of Active Management: IR = IC · √breadth · TC
  • IR +0.46 — the book adds value over its benchmark: it earned +3.68% excess CAGR per 8.0% of tracking error.
  • IC +0.037 (t 2.9) — the selection signal is genuinely informative; ~0.05 is a good single-name forecast correlation.
  • TC 0.87 — about 87% of the raw signal survives the long-only / position-cap constraints (the rest is the implementation leak).
  • vs real Aditya Birla Sun Life Midcap Fund - Growth - Direct Plan — the paper book ran 5.43% ahead of the actual fund over 11.4 years.
IC = mean cross-sectional Spearman(ARM score, next-rebalance return) over the candidate universe; TC = mean corr(actual target weights, unconstrained score-weights); BR is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are NOT independent — true breadth is far lower), so implied_IR is an upper bound on what the signal could deliver, to be read against the realized IR.
Definitions — IC · Breadth · TC · IR
IC (information coefficient) = the rank correlation between the signal's forecast and the realised next-period return, per bet — how often the call is right. Breadth (BR) = the number of independent bets per year — more, de-correlated bets compound skill. TC (transfer coefficient) = the fraction of that skill that actually reaches the live portfolio after long-only and position-size constraints. IR (information ratio) = excess return ÷ tracking error — the realised skill the law predicts as IC·√BR·TC. Breadth here is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are not independent), so implied IR is a ceiling, not a forecast.

Plain-English read — Fundamental Law of Active Management: IR = IC · √breadth · TC
  • IR +0.48 — the book adds value over its benchmark: it earned +7.84% excess CAGR per 16.3% of tracking error.
  • IC +0.044 (t 4.7) — the selection signal is genuinely informative; ~0.05 is a good single-name forecast correlation.
  • TC 0.40 — about 40% of the raw signal survives the long-only / position-cap constraints (the rest is the implementation leak).
  • vs real Aditya Birla Sun Life MNC Fund - Growth - Direct Plan — the paper book ran 11.09% ahead of the actual fund over 11.4 years.
IC = mean cross-sectional Spearman(ARM score, next-rebalance return) over the candidate universe; TC = mean corr(actual target weights, unconstrained score-weights); BR is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are NOT independent — true breadth is far lower), so implied_IR is an upper bound on what the signal could deliver, to be read against the realized IR.
Definitions — IC · Breadth · TC · IR
IC (information coefficient) = the rank correlation between the signal's forecast and the realised next-period return, per bet — how often the call is right. Breadth (BR) = the number of independent bets per year — more, de-correlated bets compound skill. TC (transfer coefficient) = the fraction of that skill that actually reaches the live portfolio after long-only and position-size constraints. IR (information ratio) = excess return ÷ tracking error — the realised skill the law predicts as IC·√BR·TC. Breadth here is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are not independent), so implied IR is a ceiling, not a forecast.

Plain-English read — Fundamental Law of Active Management: IR = IC · √breadth · TC
  • IR +0.21 — the book edges its benchmark: it earned +1.62% excess CAGR per 7.7% of tracking error.
  • IC +0.047 (t 5.0) — the selection signal is genuinely informative; ~0.05 is a good single-name forecast correlation.
  • TC 0.76 — about 76% of the raw signal survives the long-only / position-cap constraints (the rest is the implementation leak).
IC = mean cross-sectional Spearman(ARM score, next-rebalance return) over the candidate universe; TC = mean corr(actual target weights, unconstrained score-weights); BR is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are NOT independent — true breadth is far lower), so implied_IR is an upper bound on what the signal could deliver, to be read against the realized IR.
Definitions — IC · Breadth · TC · IR
IC (information coefficient) = the rank correlation between the signal's forecast and the realised next-period return, per bet — how often the call is right. Breadth (BR) = the number of independent bets per year — more, de-correlated bets compound skill. TC (transfer coefficient) = the fraction of that skill that actually reaches the live portfolio after long-only and position-size constraints. IR (information ratio) = excess return ÷ tracking error — the realised skill the law predicts as IC·√BR·TC. Breadth here is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are not independent), so implied IR is a ceiling, not a forecast.

Plain-English read — Fundamental Law of Active Management: IR = IC · √breadth · TC
  • IR +0.77 — the book adds value over its benchmark: it earned +10.49% excess CAGR per 13.7% of tracking error.
  • IC +0.042 (t 4.9) — the selection signal is genuinely informative; ~0.05 is a good single-name forecast correlation.
  • TC 0.41 — about 40% of the raw signal survives the long-only / position-cap constraints (the rest is the implementation leak).
  • vs real Aditya Birla Sun Life Multi-Cap Fund-Direct Growth — the paper book ran 7.25% ahead of the actual fund over 5.1 years.
IC = mean cross-sectional Spearman(ARM score, next-rebalance return) over the candidate universe; TC = mean corr(actual target weights, unconstrained score-weights); BR is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are NOT independent — true breadth is far lower), so implied_IR is an upper bound on what the signal could deliver, to be read against the realized IR.
Definitions — IC · Breadth · TC · IR
IC (information coefficient) = the rank correlation between the signal's forecast and the realised next-period return, per bet — how often the call is right. Breadth (BR) = the number of independent bets per year — more, de-correlated bets compound skill. TC (transfer coefficient) = the fraction of that skill that actually reaches the live portfolio after long-only and position-size constraints. IR (information ratio) = excess return ÷ tracking error — the realised skill the law predicts as IC·√BR·TC. Breadth here is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are not independent), so implied IR is a ceiling, not a forecast.

Plain-English read — Fundamental Law of Active Management: IR = IC · √breadth · TC
  • IR +0.98 — the book adds value over its benchmark: it earned +10.07% excess CAGR per 10.2% of tracking error.
  • IC +0.043 (t 2.7) — the selection signal is genuinely informative; ~0.05 is a good single-name forecast correlation.
  • TC 0.84 — about 84% of the raw signal survives the long-only / position-cap constraints (the rest is the implementation leak).
  • vs real Aditya Birla Sun Life Pharma and Healthcare Fund-Direct-Growth — the paper book ran 9.09% ahead of the actual fund over 7.0 years.
IC = mean cross-sectional Spearman(ARM score, next-rebalance return) over the candidate universe; TC = mean corr(actual target weights, unconstrained score-weights); BR is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are NOT independent — true breadth is far lower), so implied_IR is an upper bound on what the signal could deliver, to be read against the realized IR.
Definitions — IC · Breadth · TC · IR
IC (information coefficient) = the rank correlation between the signal's forecast and the realised next-period return, per bet — how often the call is right. Breadth (BR) = the number of independent bets per year — more, de-correlated bets compound skill. TC (transfer coefficient) = the fraction of that skill that actually reaches the live portfolio after long-only and position-size constraints. IR (information ratio) = excess return ÷ tracking error — the realised skill the law predicts as IC·√BR·TC. Breadth here is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are not independent), so implied IR is a ceiling, not a forecast.

Plain-English read — Fundamental Law of Active Management: IR = IC · √breadth · TC
  • IR +0.33 — the book adds value over its benchmark: it earned +5.33% excess CAGR per 16.0% of tracking error.
  • IC +0.044 (t 4.7) — the selection signal is genuinely informative; ~0.05 is a good single-name forecast correlation.
  • TC 0.37 — about 37% of the raw signal survives the long-only / position-cap constraints (the rest is the implementation leak).
  • vs real Aditya Birla Sun Life PSU Equity Fund-Direct Plan-Growth — the paper book ran 0.73% behind the actual fund over 6.5 years.
IC = mean cross-sectional Spearman(ARM score, next-rebalance return) over the candidate universe; TC = mean corr(actual target weights, unconstrained score-weights); BR is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are NOT independent — true breadth is far lower), so implied_IR is an upper bound on what the signal could deliver, to be read against the realized IR.
Definitions — IC · Breadth · TC · IR
IC (information coefficient) = the rank correlation between the signal's forecast and the realised next-period return, per bet — how often the call is right. Breadth (BR) = the number of independent bets per year — more, de-correlated bets compound skill. TC (transfer coefficient) = the fraction of that skill that actually reaches the live portfolio after long-only and position-size constraints. IR (information ratio) = excess return ÷ tracking error — the realised skill the law predicts as IC·√BR·TC. Breadth here is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are not independent), so implied IR is a ceiling, not a forecast.

Plain-English read — Fundamental Law of Active Management: IR = IC · √breadth · TC
  • IR +0.55 — the book adds value over its benchmark: it earned +8.91% excess CAGR per 16.3% of tracking error.
  • IC +0.044 (t 4.7) — the selection signal is genuinely informative; ~0.05 is a good single-name forecast correlation.

IC = mean cross-sectional Spearman(ARM score, next-rebalance return) over the candidate universe; TC = mean corr(actual target weights, unconstrained score-weights); BR is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are NOT independent — true breadth is far lower), so implied_IR is an upper bound on what the signal could deliver, to be read against the realized IR.
Definitions — IC · Breadth · TC · IR
IC (information coefficient) = the rank correlation between the signal's forecast and the realised next-period return, per bet — how often the call is right. Breadth (BR) = the number of independent bets per year — more, de-correlated bets compound skill. TC (transfer coefficient) = the fraction of that skill that actually reaches the live portfolio after long-only and position-size constraints. IR (information ratio) = excess return ÷ tracking error — the realised skill the law predicts as IC·√BR·TC. Breadth here is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are not independent), so implied IR is a ceiling, not a forecast.

Plain-English read — Fundamental Law of Active Management: IR = IC · √breadth · TC
  • IR +0.61 — the book adds value over its benchmark: it earned +9.81% excess CAGR per 16.2% of tracking error.
  • IC +0.044 (t 4.7) — the selection signal is genuinely informative; ~0.05 is a good single-name forecast correlation.
  • TC 0.49 — about 49% of the raw signal survives the long-only / position-cap constraints (the rest is the implementation leak).
  • vs real Aditya Birla Sun Life Special Opportunities Fund-Direct-Growth — the paper book ran 6.51% ahead of the actual fund over 5.7 years.
IC = mean cross-sectional Spearman(ARM score, next-rebalance return) over the candidate universe; TC = mean corr(actual target weights, unconstrained score-weights); BR is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are NOT independent — true breadth is far lower), so implied_IR is an upper bound on what the signal could deliver, to be read against the realized IR.
Definitions — IC · Breadth · TC · IR
IC (information coefficient) = the rank correlation between the signal's forecast and the realised next-period return, per bet — how often the call is right. Breadth (BR) = the number of independent bets per year — more, de-correlated bets compound skill. TC (transfer coefficient) = the fraction of that skill that actually reaches the live portfolio after long-only and position-size constraints. IR (information ratio) = excess return ÷ tracking error — the realised skill the law predicts as IC·√BR·TC. Breadth here is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are not independent), so implied IR is a ceiling, not a forecast.

Plain-English read — Fundamental Law of Active Management: IR = IC · √breadth · TC
  • IR +1.39 — the book adds value over its benchmark: it earned +19.05% excess CAGR per 13.8% of tracking error.
  • IC +0.058 (t 5.8) — the selection signal is genuinely informative; ~0.05 is a good single-name forecast correlation.
  • TC 0.73 — about 73% of the raw signal survives the long-only / position-cap constraints (the rest is the implementation leak).
IC = mean cross-sectional Spearman(ARM score, next-rebalance return) over the candidate universe; TC = mean corr(actual target weights, unconstrained score-weights); BR is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are NOT independent — true breadth is far lower), so implied_IR is an upper bound on what the signal could deliver, to be read against the realized IR.
Definitions — IC · Breadth · TC · IR
IC (information coefficient) = the rank correlation between the signal's forecast and the realised next-period return, per bet — how often the call is right. Breadth (BR) = the number of independent bets per year — more, de-correlated bets compound skill. TC (transfer coefficient) = the fraction of that skill that actually reaches the live portfolio after long-only and position-size constraints. IR (information ratio) = excess return ÷ tracking error — the realised skill the law predicts as IC·√BR·TC. Breadth here is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are not independent), so implied IR is a ceiling, not a forecast.

Plain-English read — Fundamental Law of Active Management: IR = IC · √breadth · TC
  • IR +0.24 — the book edges its benchmark: it earned +2.32% excess CAGR per 9.8% of tracking error.
  • IC +0.037 (t 2.4) — the selection signal is genuinely informative; ~0.05 is a good single-name forecast correlation.
  • TC 0.82 — about 82% of the raw signal survives the long-only / position-cap constraints (the rest is the implementation leak).
  • vs real ICICI Prudential Large Cap Fund (erstwhile Bluechip Fund) - Direct Plan - Growth — the paper book ran 0.67% ahead of the actual fund over 11.4 years.
IC = mean cross-sectional Spearman(ARM score, next-rebalance return) over the candidate universe; TC = mean corr(actual target weights, unconstrained score-weights); BR is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are NOT independent — true breadth is far lower), so implied_IR is an upper bound on what the signal could deliver, to be read against the realized IR.
Definitions — IC · Breadth · TC · IR
IC (information coefficient) = the rank correlation between the signal's forecast and the realised next-period return, per bet — how often the call is right. Breadth (BR) = the number of independent bets per year — more, de-correlated bets compound skill. TC (transfer coefficient) = the fraction of that skill that actually reaches the live portfolio after long-only and position-size constraints. IR (information ratio) = excess return ÷ tracking error — the realised skill the law predicts as IC·√BR·TC. Breadth here is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are not independent), so implied IR is a ceiling, not a forecast.

Plain-English read — Fundamental Law of Active Management: IR = IC · √breadth · TC
  • IR +0.92 — the book adds value over its benchmark: it earned +5.56% excess CAGR per 6.0% of tracking error.
  • IC +0.045 (t 5.0) — the selection signal is genuinely informative; ~0.05 is a good single-name forecast correlation.
  • TC 0.43 — about 43% of the raw signal survives the long-only / position-cap constraints (the rest is the implementation leak).
  • vs real quant Small Cap Fund - Growth Option - Direct Plan — the paper book ran 0.50% ahead of the actual fund over 11.4 years.
IC = mean cross-sectional Spearman(ARM score, next-rebalance return) over the candidate universe; TC = mean corr(actual target weights, unconstrained score-weights); BR is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are NOT independent — true breadth is far lower), so implied_IR is an upper bound on what the signal could deliver, to be read against the realized IR.
Definitions — IC · Breadth · TC · IR
IC (information coefficient) = the rank correlation between the signal's forecast and the realised next-period return, per bet — how often the call is right. Breadth (BR) = the number of independent bets per year — more, de-correlated bets compound skill. TC (transfer coefficient) = the fraction of that skill that actually reaches the live portfolio after long-only and position-size constraints. IR (information ratio) = excess return ÷ tracking error — the realised skill the law predicts as IC·√BR·TC. Breadth here is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are not independent), so implied IR is a ceiling, not a forecast.

Plain-English read — Fundamental Law of Active Management: IR = IC · √breadth · TC
  • IR +0.34 — the book adds value over its benchmark: it earned +2.43% excess CAGR per 7.1% of tracking error.
  • IC +0.047 (t 5.0) — the selection signal is genuinely informative; ~0.05 is a good single-name forecast correlation.
  • TC 0.61 — about 61% of the raw signal survives the long-only / position-cap constraints (the rest is the implementation leak).
IC = mean cross-sectional Spearman(ARM score, next-rebalance return) over the candidate universe; TC = mean corr(actual target weights, unconstrained score-weights); BR is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are NOT independent — true breadth is far lower), so implied_IR is an upper bound on what the signal could deliver, to be read against the realized IR.
Definitions — IC · Breadth · TC · IR
IC (information coefficient) = the rank correlation between the signal's forecast and the realised next-period return, per bet — how often the call is right. Breadth (BR) = the number of independent bets per year — more, de-correlated bets compound skill. TC (transfer coefficient) = the fraction of that skill that actually reaches the live portfolio after long-only and position-size constraints. IR (information ratio) = excess return ÷ tracking error — the realised skill the law predicts as IC·√BR·TC. Breadth here is an UPPER bound (monthly holdings are not independent), so implied IR is a ceiling, not a forecast.

Live-Forward — the LLM fund managers take the seat as of 2026-07-31 · from the seam on, the agents decide; a deterministic guardrail enforces the mandate
How to read Live-Forward
The historical track was built by the deterministic rules-FM. From the latest data date forward, the LLM fund-manager agents read their desk (the inherited book + a candidate universe with validated signals + the rules-FM target as a reference) and set a genuine conviction target book; a deterministic guardrail then clips to the mandate / liquidity / equity-floor. Every bet is pre-registered with a falsifier (anti-hindsight), it is paper-money only with no look-ahead, and the committed audit trail carries no licensed analyst values. Skill will be scored — once next month's data lands — by whether the pre-registered theses played out, via the Fundamental Law (IC·√breadth·TC).
CIO — firm review of this round
Strongest objection first: every FM correctly diagnosed a breadth failure INSIDE their own book, and then all four rebuilt on the SAME forecast — so the firm has re-created at the firm level the exact error each desk just fixed at the scheme level. All four books now run one alpha model, "cheapness earns weight only where analyst revisions are rising; cut extended price momentum," differing mainly by market cap. Three of four independently put ONGC, COFORGE and MUTHOOTFIN in their disclosed top eight, and the shared cluster widens to ASIANPAINT, TCS, GRASIM, NMDC, NATIONALUM and CHENNPETRO. Nominal firm breadth is 183 names across four desks; true breadth is closer to two independent bets (a large/mid revisions-confirmed-value bet, and Quant's small-cap three-way-confirmed bet), and that second desk is de-correlated by MANDATE, not by independent thinking. Worse, ABSL's style correction (large+mid 37%→48%) is a good scheme-level fix that moves it TOWARD the other two large-cap books, so it lowers ABSL's tracking risk while lowering firm breadth. Second objection: this is n=1. On books of 40-60 names the one-round standard error of a rank IC is about 1/sqrt(n-1), roughly 0.15 — so ABSL's +0.121 and the three negative/zero conviction ICs are all statistically indistinguishable from zero, yet the desks have written 212 tickets against 183 target names on that single round of evidence. The transaction cost is certain; the IC improvement is a hypothesis. Third, and the one I'd escalate tonight: three of four FMs independently refused the quant baseline's top picks for the same reasons — z-scores 10-40x beyond the real distribution, no analyst coverage, null flows, ETF tickers presented as companies, and a large-cap insurer sitting in the small-cap candidate set. That is not four judgments, it is one broken scoring layer that every desk is being served, and it only stayed out of the books because these particular FMs were skeptical. What I like: the reasoning quality is genuinely high, the diagnoses are honest and self-incriminating, refuted theses are being closed rather than averaged down, and every book is inside its mandate bands. The firm's problem this round is not stock selection — it is that the sizing layer, the data plane, and the shared-factor load are CIO responsibilities that no FM can fix from inside their own book.
⚠ Risk flags
  • SHARED-FACTOR CONCENTRATION [Certain, on disclosed lists]: ONGC, COFORGE and MUTHOOTFIN each appear in the top-8 of three of four schemes; the shared cluster extends to ASIANPAINT, TCS, GRASIM, NMDC, NATIONALUM, CHENNPETRO. Firm aggregate exposure to each is UNCOMPUTABLE right now because I have no scheme AUMs — the single most important missing CIO instrument is an AUM-weighted firm-consolidated book with per-name aggregate weight and days-to-liquidate.
  • THE HYBRID IS THE WHALE [Likely]: SBI states its own book is ~86,000cr, so firm-level exposure to the shared cyclical core is set mostly by ONE FM's sizing, not by four independent votes. A 3.2% ONGC position there (~2,750cr) probably dwarfs ICICI's nominally larger 5.2%. Equal-weighting the four stances materially understates concentration.
  • ONE MACRO PATH HITS THREE BOOKS [Certain, by construction]: ONGC, OIL, COALINDIA, NMDC, SAIL, HINDALCO, NATIONALUM and CHENNPETRO are a single global-growth/commodity-price trade held simultaneously by ICICI Pru, SBI Hybrid and ABSL Flexi. A crude-plus-industrial-metals deflation scare marks all three down together. Nobody OWNED this decision; it was assembled bottom-up from a screen.
  • THE HEDGE LEG IS ALSO A CLUSTER [Likely]: the shared 'quality with rising revisions' ballast is IT services (COFORGE in three books, TCS in two, TECHM in one). IT is itself one macro factor — US discretionary tech spend and USD/INR — so the offset against the commodity leg is partial at best, and both legs are long global growth.
  • NO SHOCK ABSORBER [Certain]: ICICI 95% equity, ABSL 95%, Quant 93%. The only risk-off expression in the entire firm is the hybrid's ~10.5pp of unused equity room. If the shared revisions/cyclical bet fails, there is nothing at firm level to cushion it.
  • THE LARGEST RISK ALLOCATION IN THE AMC IS UNDISCUSSED [Certain]: SBI Hybrid's ~30.5% non-equity sleeve is roughly 26,000cr and no view on duration, credit quality or curve position appears anywhere in the stance. The FM justified holding equity BELOW the ceiling on timing humility but never said what the money is doing instead. Ask for the debt-leg stance before approving.
  • DATA-PLANE DEFECT, NOT A PORTFOLIO ISSUE [Certain, from three concordant FM reports]: the baseline scoring layer is serving ETF/AMC tickers as investable companies, extreme-outlier z-scores 10-40x beyond the real distribution, at least one large-cap insurer classified into the small-cap bucket, and — per Quant — outliers dominating the cross-sectional normalisation so mainstream names' value and momentum scores collapse to ZERO, leaving the baseline as a pure revisions bet repeated sixty times. Fix upstream: winsorise or rank-normalise before z-scoring, exclude fund/ETF tickers from the equity universe, enforce a market-cap-bucket check, and gate any weight above a starter size on minimum analyst coverage.
  • SIGNAL-DECAY vs CAPACITY MISMATCH [Likely]: Quant characterises revisions as a genuine but small one-to-six-month tilt. The firm has just concentrated its dominant common exposure in a fast-decaying signal and is expressing it partly through an 86,000cr book. That is a transfer-coefficient (TC) problem, not an IC problem — the bigger the book, the less of a short-horizon revisions edge survives implementation.
  • CROWDING NOT YET TESTED ON THE NEW CLUSTER [Certain]: the desks used net institutional selling to condemn the OLD power/capex cluster, which means they have the flow data. Nobody ran the same flow test on the NEW PSU/commodity/energy cluster they are all buying. If three of our desks found it with the same screen, so did the street. Require a flow and ownership-crowding check on the shared names before sizing is approved.
  • MANDATE COMPLIANCE — VERIFY, DO NOT ASSUME [Guessing where noted]: ICICI Pru Large Cap must hold at least 80% in the top-100 by full market cap, and its book leans on LAURUSLABS and NATIONALUM (likely outside top-100) to achieve its stated sector spread — run the compliance test on the full 37 names, not the top eight. Quant Small Cap must hold at least 65% below rank 250 and carries AIAENG and CUB, which may sit above it. Both are checks, not accusations.
  • SOFT DRIFT, THE COSTLY KIND [Likely]: ABSL Flexi lifting large+mid to 48% is correct for the scheme and bad for the firm — a flexi-cap desk that converges on the large-cap books stops being a differentiated source of return. Approve the style fix but require it be paid for by DE-correlating elsewhere, not by hugging.
  • SMALL-CAP SLEEVE IS NOW A SINGLE POINT OF FAILURE [Certain]: with ABSL stepping back from small caps, the firm's entire small-cap exposure sits in the one desk that just reported NEGATIVE conviction IC and that says its own signal plane is degraded. Cleaner attribution, higher single-desk dependency.
  • NEWLY-LISTED NAMES SIZED ON A HISTORY-DEPENDENT SIGNAL [Likely]: LENSKART at 3.7% (ABSL) and SHADOWFAX at 2.9% (Quant) are recent listings with short revision histories, thin coverage and unproven free float. Sizing them at 3%-plus on a revisions-confirmation framework is a methodology mismatch — cap recent listings at starter weight until they have enough revision history for the signal to mean anything.
  • TURNOVER PAID AGAINST UNPROVEN EVIDENCE [Certain]: 212 tickets across 183 target names, driven by one graded round whose ICs are inside the noise band. Cost is realised immediately; the benefit is a conjecture.
Cross-scheme breadth
  • METHOD AND CAVEAT: overlap below is computed from each FM's disclosed top-8 targets plus names cited in their prose. I found no on-disk artifact of this round's full books (searched the project root and C:/Users/Administrator/Documents/Projects/Vistas/data/), so every overlap count is a LOWER BOUND — the true shared exposure across the full 183 names is higher, possibly much higher.
  • UNANIMOUS ON THE DIAGNOSIS: all four desks independently concluded that last round failed on SIZING and BREADTH, not on name selection — three report negative or roughly zero conviction IC, and ABSL reports positive IC (+0.121) destroyed by an unintended small-cap factor. That is a coherent firm-level finding: the loss is in the weighting layer, not the ranking layer. It also means a firm-wide sizing protocol will do more good than any amount of further stock work.
  • UNANIMOUS ON THE REMEDY — AND THAT IS THE PROBLEM: all four adopted the identical rule, buy cheap only where revisions are rising, refuse cheap-with-falling-revisions, cut unconfirmed momentum. Four desks running one forecast model is one bet expressed four ways. Under IR = IC x sqrt(BR) x TC the firm's BR is the number of INDEPENDENT bets, so nominal breadth of 183 names across four schemes collapses to roughly 2. This is the same illusory-breadth error each FM just corrected inside their own book, now reproduced one level up.
  • HARD SHARED NAMES (three of four, all in top-8): ONGC (5.2 / 3.2 / 3.3), COFORGE (3.2 / 2.6 / 5.0), MUTHOOTFIN (3.8 / 2.4 / 3.9) across ICICI Pru, SBI Hybrid and ABSL Flexi. Quant Small Cap is excluded by mandate, not by disagreement — so on the investable overlap, agreement on these three is effectively total.
  • SECOND RING OF SHARED NAMES (two of four): ASIANPAINT, TCS, GRASIM, NMDC, NATIONALUM, CHENNPETRO, plus COALINDIA / HINDALCO / SAIL sitting inside SBI's cyclical core and echoed in ABSL's adds. The large/mid sleeve of the firm is close to one portfolio.
  • UNANIMOUS ON THE REFUSAL, WHICH IS THE FIRM'S BEST SHARED CALL: ICICI refuses cheap PSU banks on falling revisions; SBI explicitly refuses IOC, HINDPETRO, BPCL, TMPV, PNB, BANKINDIA — the cheapest names in the universe — on the same grounds and calls it its highest-conviction deviation. Two desks, same falsifiable claim. TREAT IT AS A FIRM-LEVEL PRE-REGISTERED EXPERIMENT: measure the paired spread of 'cheap with rising revisions' minus 'cheap with falling revisions' over the next 3-6 months, so the firm learns something whether or not the market goes up. Right now this is the single most informative thing the firm is doing and nobody is scoring it.
  • UNANIMOUS ON DISTRUSTING THE BASELINE: ICICI drops the baseline's largest pick (a six-sigma momentum outlier with no coverage); ABSL refuses CMPDI, NIRLON, HAWKINS, TRANSPEK, RAJESH EXPORTS and two ETF tickers; Quant declines the baseline's top two and rejects two ETFs and the illiquid normalisation artifacts. Three independent desks reporting the same defect is diagnostic, not coincidental — escalate to the data layer, do not congratulate the FMs and move on.
  • GENUINE DIVERGENCE, THE HEALTHY KIND — SMALL LENDERS: ABSL is CUTTING the small-lender cluster from 23% to 17% (exiting J&K Bank, Piramal, Fusion, Satin; trimming KTKBANK, CUB, CREDITACC, EQUITAS) on correlation grounds, while Quant is ADDING KTKBANK at 3.3% and CREDITACC at 3.1% on three-way confirmation and runs lenders at 21%. This is real de-correlation and I want to keep it — but it should be an explicit, adjudicated disagreement with a stated test, not two desks quietly netting each other out. Note both agree on trimming CUB, so the disagreement is narrower than it looks.
  • GENUINE DIVERGENCE, POSSIBLY THE SAME NAME: ABSL is ADDING LICI at 3.0% as part of its large/mid spine; Quant declines what it describes as a large-cap insurer mis-tagged into the small bucket carrying the largest fund outflow in its candidate set. If that is LICI, the firm has one desk buying on rising revisions and another rejecting on flow. Resolve it with the ownership and flow data — we have it. Either way it confirms the market-cap classification defect.
  • WHERE THE DESKS ARE ACTUALLY DIFFERENT: only Quant Small Cap is running a distinct forecast — it requires THREE independent confirmations (revisions AND net active mutual-fund buying AND the position already working) before real weight, rather than revisions alone. That is the most methodologically advanced stance in the room and the only one that raises firm breadth rather than consuming it. Consider porting the multi-evidence sizing gate to the other three desks as the firm-wide answer to the shared negative conviction IC.
  • SIZING RESPONSES DIVERGE AND SHOULD BE ADJUDICATED: SBI WIDENS weight dispersion (3.2% top vs 0.9% tail) to give sizing a chance to carry information; Quant COMPRESSES the top of the book (4.0% against a 5.0% cap) to stop sizing doing damage. Both are defensible responses to the same negative-IC finding and they are opposite. Let both run as a deliberate firm-level A/B and score the sizing layer separately from the selection layer next round.
  • DISCIPLINE IS UNEVEN: ABSL and Quant both cite PRE-REGISTERED falsifiers and close refuted theses (ABSL deletes POCL, THANGAMAYIL, GRINDWELL, IOLCP; Quant exits the lead-recycler, solar modules and transformer capex). ICICI and SBI describe no falsifier at all. Make pre-registration mandatory for all four desks — without it, next round's grading cannot separate skill from hindsight.
  • THE HONEST BREADTH VERDICT: nominal 4 desks / 183 names; effective roughly 2 independent bets, and ABSL's style correction pushed the number DOWN this round rather than up. Do not fix this by asking FMs to hold more names — they have already shown that adding correlated names buys nothing. Fix it by giving desks different FORECAST inputs (flow, ownership, earnings-call change, economic-links lead-lag) so their ICs are drawn from genuinely different information, and by making a shared-name budget explicit before the next rebalance.

Risk-controlled large-cap core: collapse the crowded power/capex momentum cluster, redeploy into cheap-with-rising-revisions energy, quality financials, and lagging-price IT.
Last round graded out at a coin-flip hit rate (48.8%), slightly negative average active return, and — the number that matters — a NEGATIVE conviction IC. My biggest weights were my biggest losers. Diagnosing it honestly: four of the five worst calls were the same bet held under four tickers (expensive, extended-momentum power/electrical-capex names with heavy net institutional selling). Nominally 43 holdings; in independent-bet terms, far fewer. Under IR = IC x sqrt(BR) x TC that is a breadth failure, not a forecast failure, and no amount of better name-picking fixes it. So this rebalance does three things. (1) It collapses the capex/electricals cluster to a single, least-extended representative and exits every position whose only support is an extreme price-momentum reading with no analyst-revision corroboration — including the quant baseline's own largest pick, whose score is driven almost entirely by a six-sigma momentum outlier in a name analysts do not cover. That single-input sizing is exactly what produced the negative conviction IC. (2) It rebuilds weight into the profile that actually paid: names where analyst revisions are strong and RISING while price momentum still lags. That was the shape of my four best calls, and it is a forecastable dislocation rather than a crowded trade. (3) It applies one discipline to the value side — cheapness only earns a seat when revisions are also rising. That keeps me long cheap energy and metals with revision support, and keeps me out of the deeply cheap PSU banks the baseline likes, where revisions are falling (the value-trap signature). Net result: 37 names, roughly 95% equity, top weight ~5% (half the per-name cap), and deliberate spread across energy, financials, IT, metals, staples, pharma, consumer discretionary, real estate and internet so that the bets are genuinely independent rather than nine expressions of one macro view.

The usable structure in this candidate set is not "value" — it is the split INSIDE the cheap bucket. Energy and PSU financials hold nearly all the cheapness, but the analyst-revision signal separates them cleanly: upstream oil and one refiner carry strong, rising revisions, while the large downstream refiners are the very cheapest names in the universe AND carry the most sharply falling revisions in it. So I buy cheapness only where revisions confirm it (ONGC, CHENNPETRO, OIL, COALINDIA, NMDC, SAIL, HINDALCO) and deliberately skip the cheapest names in the universe where revisions are collapsing (IOC, HINDPETRO, BPCL, TMPV, PNB, BANKINDIA), even though the quant baseline wants several of them — cheap plus falling revisions is a value trap, and refusing it is the single highest-conviction deviation I am making. Against that cyclical core I hold a barbell of liquid quality with rising revisions (COFORGE, TCS, TECHM, BAJAJ-AUTO, ASIANPAINT, NESTLEIND, GRASIM, MUTHOOTFIN, CHOLAFIN) because my benchmark's equity leg is a large-cap index and, on an 86,000cr book, a 1% position is 860cr — signal I cannot execute is not alpha, it is a transfer leak. Last round graded at -0.7% average active return with a conviction-IC of essentially zero, meaning my sizing carried no information at all; the response is to widen weight dispersion sharply (3.2% top name vs 0.9% tail) so that sizing has a chance to express a view rather than being noise, and to cut the holdings count from 49 to 44 by removing the names that were both refuted and too small to matter. Equity sits at ~69.5% — above the 65% floor but well short of the 80% ceiling, because valuation dispersion this wide usually means the cheap side re-rates violently in both directions, and I have just been shown my own timing is not sharp enough to earn maximum exposure.

Last round graded my book at a 36% hit rate and −2.91% average active return against a +1.1% benchmark, yet my conviction-IC was POSITIVE (+0.121). Read honestly, that says my ranking of names had some skill while a single undiversified exposure ate all of it: only ~37% of the book sat in large/mid buckets against a large-cap-dominated NIFTY 500, so 55 nominal bets behaved like one bet on small caps. The fix is not to abandon the small/mid alpha source — that is what a flexi-cap mandate is for — but to stop paying for it with unintended factor risk. I lift large+mid from ~37% to ~48% by adding to COFORGE, LENSKART, GRASIM, ONGC, ASIAN PAINTS, LICI, NMDC and NATIONALUM, all of which carry rising analyst revisions in their own right, so the de-risking is not a sacrifice of conviction. Second, I cut the crowded lending cluster (small banks, NBFCs, microfinance) from ~23% to ~17% by exiting J&K BANK, PIRAMAL FINANCE, FUSION and SATIN and trimming KARNATAKA BANK, CITY UNION, CREDITACCESS and EQUITAS — those names are near-duplicates of one another and their correlation was the hidden reason my breadth was illusory. Third, I delete the sub-scale tail (SUPRAJIT, PRINCE PIPES, DBL) and every name my own pre-registered falsifier flagged last round (POCL, THANGAMAYIL, GRINDWELL, IOLCP), on the discipline that a refuted thesis is closed, not averaged down. I keep and add to what worked — COFORGE, NAZARA, SENCO, RELAXO, and NILKAMAL, my best call which I had criminally undersized at 0.15%. Two genuinely new names only: BLUE JET HEALTHCARE (cheap on the blended value screen with constructive revisions) and MAHINDRA LIFESPACE (a real-estate exposure I do not otherwise own). I explicitly REFUSE the quant baseline's top pick, CMPDI, and the whole cluster of extreme-score names above it — NIRLON, HAWKINS, TRANSPEK, RAJESH EXPORTS, and the two entries that are AMC exchange-traded-fund tickers rather than companies at all. Their valuation and momentum z-scores sit ten to forty times beyond the real distribution with no analyst coverage and null flows; that is a data artifact, and buying it is exactly how POCL got into this book. Result: 45 names (band is 40-70), top position 5.0% against a 9% cap, ~95% equity, ~5% cash.

My grade this round says the problem was sizing, not stock-picking: conviction IC was negative and the median bet did worse than the mean, meaning my largest positions were my worst and my best call was sized at almost nothing. So the book changes shape more than it changes names. Second, I have to be honest about the signal plane I am handed: for essentially every mainstream candidate the momentum and cheapness scores collapse to zero because a few implausible outliers dominate the cross-sectional normalisation, so the quant baseline's ranking is very close to a pure analyst-revision bet repeated sixty times. Revisions are a genuine but small one-to-six-month tilt, and sixty copies of the same tilt is one bet, not sixty - true breadth is far below the holding count, so adding more revision-only names buys nothing. My response is to require agreement across independent evidence before sizing up: strong revisions AND real net active mutual-fund buying AND the position actually working. Six names clear that bar and get 3.0-4.0% (Poonawalla, Nazara, Karnataka Bank, Honasa, CreditAccess, City Union); ten more get 2.4-2.9%; the mandated tail is held deliberately small rather than pretending it carries conviction. I keep the top weight at 4.0% against a 5.0% cap on purpose. I exit the cohort my own falsifiers flagged - the lead-recycling blow-up, solar module manufacturing, and transformer capex - and I halve, rather than defend, the domestic EPC and stressed-microfinance exposure. I lean into what actually worked, jewellery and gold retail and third-party logistics, but add less than the move would justify because buying after a thirty-percent two-week pop is itself a risk. I decline the baseline's top two picks: one is a large-cap insurer mis-tagged into the small bucket with the largest fund outflow in the set, and the other is a single extreme cheapness score with no coverage, no momentum and no flow to corroborate it, which I take as a one-percent starter rather than a top weight. I also reject the two exchange-traded funds and the illiquid names whose scores are normalisation artifacts. Roughly 93% invested across 57 names, lenders about 21% against a 30% cap.

How to read this
An experimental, paper-money research firm: agents — sector analysts, fund managers, a CIO — read the terminal's real data and produce grounded views. Every view cites the actual numbers (ARM 0–100 analyst-revision momentum, net fund flows in ₹cr, growth, real fund IR/IC). Agents synthesize validated signals into judgment; they do not manufacture alpha. Skill is judged by the Fundamental Law of Active Management (IR = IC·√breadth·TC): analysts on IC, managers on IR (and the transfer-coefficient leak), the firm on breadth.
Not investment advice. Generated 2026-06-26 · data as of 2026-05.

Net positioning is roughly market-neutral on beta with quality/earnings-momentum tilts: overweight where ARM, fund flow and PAT all confirm (Q1) AND the name is genuinely large-cap, modest underweights where the signal is a Q4 warning, and benchmark-weight on the index anchors I have no edge on. Investor experience
My north star is a sittable path, not the highest CAGR. Because my desk's revealed IC is ~0, I will NOT manufacture alpha through concentration -- I spread the small ARM/flow tilt across 6-10 independent large-cap overweights (breadth) and keep single-name active weight bounded so tracking error stays ~2.5-3.0% (in line with exemplars ICICI Pru 3.0, Mirae 3.1). That keeps the investor's quarter-to-quarter experience close to NIFTY 100 with a steady quality lean, targeting a hit rate in the 55-62% band the skilled exemplars show. I deliberately decline the high-octane mid/small Q1 names (Coforge, Hexaware, BSE) -- they would juice returns but breach mandate and add drawdown the large-cap investor did not sign up for. Consistency and a shallow drawdown profile come from owning index anchors near weight and only tilting where two independent forces agree.

I privilege TRIPLE-CONFIRM Quadrant-1 (analysts + funds + earnings aligned) so ARM's small IC (~0.03-0.045) is reinforced by flow/earnings, lifting the transfer coefficient rather than betting lone-ARM tilts.

🏛️ Chief Investment Officer House view
The tape is a STOCK-PICKER'S market, not a beta market. No sector ARM clears 63 float-weighted; the unweighted median sector ARM sits near 50 (Industrials 44.5 EW is the weakest, the megacap LT/ABB/Siemens drag pulling float-weight to 39.2). Edge this cycle lives almost entirely in Quadrant 1 (analysts upgrading AND funds buying), and Q1 breadth is concentrated in four desks: Financials (39 Q1 names), Diversified (37), Consumer (36) and Healthcare (28). The Fundamental Law (IR = IC x sqrt(BR) x TC) is the firm's whole edge here: per-name ARM IC is only ~0.03-0.045 on a 1-6M clock, so we win by BREADTH of independent confirmed bets and by TRANSFER (actually sizing them), never by concentration or by lone-ARM hero calls. Float-weight ARM leading equal-weight (Technology 62.4>57.6, Consumer 52.8>47.7, Materials 53.4>47.2) tells us the quality/large end is where revisions concentrate inside otherwise middling sectors -- so the standing instruction across desks is: own confirmed quality at the large/quality end, harvest mid-cap Q1 quality where flow confirms, refuse single-force tilts. Firmwide directive: triple-confirm (ARM + flow + PAT) sized as breadth; treat every loud force-divergence (VEDL, LICI) as a risk event to manage, not an alpha to chase.
3-lens market pulse — the gaps between the lenses are the signal
Street · analysts / ARM
Analysts (ARM) are selectively constructive, never broadly bullish. The only sectors with ARM above the high-50s are Telecom EW 59.4, Technology FF 62.4, Healthcare EW 56.9 and Financials EW 55.2 -- and in every one the float-weight vs equal-weight split shows upgrades are CONCENTRATED (Tech FF 62.4 > EW 57.6 = large-cap quality; Telecom EW 59.4 > FF 55.9 = the edge is in smaller media/content names, NOT heavy-telecom incumbents). Highest individual ARM prints are revision outliers funds are NOT confirming: LICI 99, ONGC 98, NAZARA 98, Bharat Forge 84, VEDL 70.
Smart money · fund flows
Fund flows tell a partly DIFFERENT story than analysts. Funds are aggressively buying large index anchors regardless of revisions -- Maruti +Rs2,559cr and Hyundai +Rs1,811cr (weak Auto ARM 46.1), RELIANCE +Rs3,801cr (neutral ARM 49), BHARTIARTL +Rs8,521cr. They are DISTRIBUTING the loud-ARM names: VEDL -Rs13,051cr against ARM 70, LICI -Rs934cr against ARM 99, LUPIN -Rs1,975cr, GLAND -Rs579cr. So smart money is paying up for liquidity/franchise and selling crowded revision stories.
Reward · price / quadrant
Quadrant behaviour (price/positioning): the largest single bucket firmwide is Quadrant 4 (both weak) -- Diversified alone has 125 of 288 names in Q4, Industrials 40, Financials 25, Materials 23. Quadrant 3 (funds buying AHEAD of analysts) is next-biggest in Consumer (44), Industrials (42), Materials (25), Energy (15) -- flow front-running revisions in cyclicals. Q1 (the reward-and-confirmation zone) is a minority everywhere except Healthcare (28/68 = the cleanest confirm-breadth on the board).
★ The gaps
THE GAPS ARE THE SIGNAL. Three structural divergences: (1) VEDL -- street says ARM 70 (healthy), smart money says -Rs13,051cr (record exodus): a gap this large = an event analysts have not marked (de-merger/overhang); trust the flow. (2) The OEM/anchor gap -- funds buying Maruti/Hyundai/Reliance where ARM is neutral-weak: liquidity/franchise demand, NOT alpha, so hold benchmark-weight, do not tilt on it. (3) LICI/ZYDUSLIFE/Bharat Forge -- analysts ahead, funds absent (Q2): revision-only, IC too thin to size alone -- wait for flow. LEVEL agreement across forces = crowding (fragile); CHANGE agreement = conviction (Q1). The reward is in CHANGE-agreement, the risk is in the LEVEL-agreement crowds.
